neighborhood_overview:
The Berlin Artist Apartment is situated in a pre-war apartment building in the heart Berlin's Friedrichshain district, east of Alexanderplatz. It is perhaps the last resort for Berlin's famous alternative subculture. The streets culture is colourful and vibrant: Left over artist squats merge with imposing monumental Stalin-era buildings. Late-nineteenth century apartment buildings, galleries, alternative bars, clubs and cafes permeate the streets. Simon Dach Strasse is a popular spot with students, artists, young families as well as young Berliners.

The front of the apartment building has a liquor and convenience shop, a fantastic bakery, café and icecream shop. Nearby Boxhagener platz hosts the fantastic farmers market on Saturday, and the famous flea market on the Sunday. Reveler Str flea market is at the end of the Street. There are a range of supermarkets nearby.

Hope to hear from you soon.
Yves

name: Center - Artist Studio with Garden
neighborhood_overview: In our area around Potsdamer Straße, you will find galleries and designer shops that are popular with art lovers and local visitors. The Kulturforum at Potsdamer Platz includes several state museums and the Berlin Philharmonic. The new National Gallery, Cultural Forum, Philharmonic Hall, State Library and Potsdamer Platz can be reached on foot in 5 - 10 minutes. You can reach the Tiergarten, one of the largest and most beautiful parks in Berlin, by bike in no more than 5 minutes. Another park is the Park am Gleisdreieck, which offers beach volleyball fields, a skate park, playgrounds and natural gardens. Culture and subculture are closely related in this area. Shrill bars like the Kumpelnest 3000 and hip fashion designers in the building complex of the former TAGESSPIEGEL publishing house shake hands. The Winter Garden on the other hand inspires visitors with constantly changing shows. Right next to it, in a beautifully restored old Berlin building with fantastically designed courtyard

Sitting in the nearby park with the lake Lietzensee reading a good book or making a picknick is my favourite way to spend my free time in the neighbourhood. The Friedbergstrasse is so quite and you are close to public transport which takes you to whichever corner of Berlin and Potsdam you fancy.
neighborhood_overview: Charlottenburg is a quite neighbourhood with buildings from the beginning of the 20th century. You only have to walk 200m to get to the Lietzensee which is surrounded by a beautiful park. You can chose between Indian, Italian, Japanese and other food in the surroundings. The S-Bahn (Charlottenburg) is 700m away, the U-Bahn, U2 Sophie Charlotte Platz 1000m, the U7 Wilmersdorfer Straße 1100m away for you to have the best connection to Berlin-Mitte and other places.

Prenzlauer Berg is characterised by old buildings, the majority of which come from the turn of the 20th century (1889 to 1905). Over 80% of all housing in this area was constructed before 1948, with the oldest building still standing being from 1848 at 77 Kastanienallee. In the second World War, relatively few buildings were destroyed in comparison to other areas of the city. The area was neglected in the time of the German Democratic Republic, and the last ruins were cleared away only at the beginning of the 1970s. After the fall of the Berlin Wall and subsequent German Reunification, the dilapidated structures in many areas were rehabilitated, and since the middle of the 1980s empty lots have been closed up.

neighborhood_overview: Charlottenburg-Westend is a beautiful and multifaceted district with a lot of tradition. You can easily reach the exhibition grounds, the Olympic Stadium and the lively Theodor-Heuss-Platz on foot. The beer garden on the stadium terraces, the radio tower, the forest stage, the voles, a bowling alley and a lot of shops and restaurants  as well as snacks and cafés are in the immediate vicinity. Actually, you do not have to leave the neighborhood for everyday errands. If you want to go to the city, start comfortably with the bus right outside the door or the metro line 2. If you want to go swimming, wait with the swimming pool at the Olympic Stadium one of the best swimming pools in the city. For walks in fresh greenery and on the Spree, the Charlottenburg Palace Park and the villa area or the beautiful old building district of the Westend await. For children there are playgrounds at the Fürstenplatz.

Berlin's Mitte district 
Here the city's past and present meet, creating a visually challenging blend. From the V buildings that are reminiscent of socialist times to charming cobbled streets, from ancient treasures to prestigious modern art. Mitte is a Mecca for shoppers and hipsters from all over the world. Surrounded by trendy shops, cafés, restaurants and the famous ‘Friedrichstrasse', one of the most famous streets in all of Berlin. Due to the partition of East and West Berlin, the Berlin wall ran directly through this street, splitting it into an ‘East-side' and a ‘West-side'. The world renowned ‘Checkpoint Charlie' was also located here – a border crossing point that became a symbol of the Cold War. It can still be seen today. Walking distance to the Jewish Synagogue, Friedrichstadtpalast, Gendamenmarkt, Brandenburger Tor, Museum Island (Museumsinsel) and Fernsehturm.

name: Well-Designed Shiny Nest in the Heart of Berlin
description: Welcome to our charming studio apartment in Prenzlauerberg, a blend of comfort and convenience, perfect for 3 guests. It features a luxurious queen bed, a versatile single sofa bed, a full kitchen, and a tranquil bathroom with a park-view bathtub. neighborhood_overview: The apartment is located in the vibrant & historic neighbourhood of Prenzlauerberg. Mauerpark, the biggest flea market in Berlin featuring the rests of the Berlin Wall, is only a walk away. Most of them are situated 5min away in Stargarderstraße where you will also find Hokey-Pokey: the best ice-cream in Berlin. The oldest bakery in Berlin Siebert Bakery is a walk away while Bäcker Kroll and Hacker Bäckerei also offer authentic german breads and cakes, DDR interiors are on the house. Only a few minutes away by foot, the UNESCO World Heritage Wohnstadt Carl Legien residential block is an entire complex in early Bauhaus style dating back to the 1920.

description: Modern and quiet penthouse studio located in the cultural heart of Berlin-Neukölln, a colorfull lively multi ethnic neighborhood with many different nationalities and cultural backgrounds. neighborhood_overview:
The area is full of students, artists and people from all sorts of cultural backgrounds and nationalities. It is becoming a vivid neighborhood full of bars, cafés and art galleries but still not so hipsterish like i.e. Prenzlberg. Here is Berlin like it always was, a colorfull mix of all kinds of inhabitants.
In walking distance you will find the Tempelhofer Feld, Berlin´s former airport build by the nazis and now Berlin´s biggest public park. Sporty people use the landing lanes for kite-boarding, skating and bike-riding. An urban gardening community turned part of the airport into a unique blossoming garden.
Two busy streets form the backbone of Neukölln, Karl-Marx-Str. and Hermannstr., both full of bustling cheap shops and eateries. The more cooler sites lay in the backstreets like Weserstr., Herrfurthplatz in the Shillerkietz, nearby Emser Str. or little father Kreuzberg and the so called Kreuzkölln, along many others.

host_about:
Dear community of travelers, 
Hi! My name is Paz, I come from Spain and I live in Berlin for 4 years now (just got the medal for winter olympics here ;-). I'm involved with the independent art scene in the city, I make projects, I meet people, I meet spaces, I make more projects, I meet more people.
I like to host and I like to move. It's a very different feeling to know a place through somebody's home: "A room of one's own" (Virginia Woolf). I like storytelling, I like objects, I like environments... They are gifts, entry points to the city through different doors, that's why I have a profile in airbnb and I like to use this platform to travel and host.
My Berliner apartment is my soul. I was very lucky, I live with two italians and one dog that just add the "extra" to the "ordinary" at home. We built the house ourselves. We learn to be patience. We embraced german non-materialistic culture, things have many lives here, if you wait, if you get lost in the second hand markets of the city, that lamp, that shelf, that armchair, that old teapot, will find their way to your home. 
I believe in the kindness of strangers. 
I like to make things special, I like details, and I have objects at home that are like little traces, hints, reminders of other people I have met, loved or admired. Things that I have lived, experiences, memories captured in small doses that complete the circle of the person I am at this moment. 
this is it! :-)

neighborhood_overview:
Schöneberg is an old and organically grown West Berlin district, diverse, lively but also quiet, central and very green – not only political.
In addition to traditional institutions such as Cafe M or Double Eye, many new shops are being built with young operators.
Children can romp around in the neighboring playgrounds or in the swimming pool 200m away, parents can relax in bars or with coffee, joggers in the Volkspark make their rounds, go hungry in the numerous restaurants or spend every Saturday at the legendary Winterfeldtmarkt. Culture and art lovers are not far from the internationally known galleries in Potsdam Street, but there are also small growing galleries all around where you can find inspiration or right next door with my wonderful neighbor.

Meine Liebe für schöne Räume, Möbel und Geschichten habe ich 2016 in den Umbau des Apartments "woanders" gesteckt. Our flat is in the middle of Berlin in the not-yet-hipster neighbourhood of Moabit. This neighbourhood is very diverse, as the old local Berlin inhabitants live here together with immigrants, students and hipsters. Prenzlauer Berg is home to art galleries, small cafés, original bars and concert halls. It is the best place for fair trade coffee, organic and vegetarian restaurants and a great place if you want to sleep in Berlin in a trendy and quiet place, like living in a small village inside of a capital.

Potsdam is close and can be reached from Kladow by bus, car or bicycle.

Along with Friedrichshain, Neukölln and Kreuzberg it is also a popular neighbourhood with the student population; however, in recent years, the gentrification that paralleled the borough's rise in popularity resulted in an exodus of students to cheaper neighborhoods. 2007 German journalist Henning Sußebach coined the term Bionade-Biedermeier, a neologism combining the name of a popular organic softdrink with the Biedermeier era (1815-1848) to describe the sociocultural situation of Prenzlauer Berg. The term is equivalent to e.g. LOHAS and Bobo (Bohémiens bourgeoises).

neighborhood_overview:
Schöneberg is a comfortable mixed neighborhood full of everything that you might want during your stay in Berlin. It was in the west during the time of the Berlin Wall and since the 1920s has been known for it's vibrant LGBTQ community. JKF plaza, where JFK made his famous "Ich bin Berliner" speech - at the Rathaus Schöneberg, is visible from our Terrace and the plaza hosts farmers markets on Tuesdays and Fridays and an enormous flee market on the weekend where you can find everything second hand you can imagine. Luxury shopping at KaDeWe is nearby, the 2-story public pool with a giant water slide is a 5 minute walk from us (recently renovated), playgrounds for young children galore, and Wannsee Lake is a 15 minute ride on the S-Bahn - so refreshing on a hot day. Notable residents of the district were Einstein, Iggy Pop, and David Bowie. I personally love all the food options. One the main road near our place is Thai, Turkish, Arabic, Sudanese, and Vietnamese. Delicious!

name: Family flat in Neukölln (direct from SXF Airport)
description:
We are German/British couple who would like to welcome you to our home in Berlin's popular Neukölln district.

Our flat is spacious with big windows letting in lots of light especially during summer. It is also very well insulated and stays nice and warm in winter. We completely renovated it in 2017 so everything is new and in great condition. It's a child-friendly home, perfect for families with smaller children as we have lots of toys. Our son's room can also double as an extra guest room.
neighborhood_overview:
Our flat is located in bustling Neukölln, a very popular and hip district in the south-east of Berlin. We are situated on a very quiet side-street near Neukölln's border with Treptow, just a one-minute walk from where the Berlin wall used to run.

Directly in front of our apartment block runs the picturesque Landwehr canal, which is lined with cafés and bars, the nearest ones being "Nah am Wasser" and "Zimt und Mehl", an excellent bakery café.

Perhaps our favourite aspect of where we live is our location within the city. Neukölln is known for its vibrant, creative, open-minded attitude which is reflected in its multicultural population as well as its restaurants, cafés and nightlife. At the same time our neighbourhood itself remains affordable and down to earth.

We are also within walking distance of Berlin's other popular districts Kreuzberg and Friedrichshain.

Shopping:
We have at least three major supermarkets within walking distance

description:
Enjoy this spacious private room located in Mitte, the city’s most central district. Complete with fresh linen, towels and toiletries this hostel is the ideal base for you to explore the culture, history and nightlife of this amazing city.

In the evenings, meet new friends at our hostel bar and party into the night! For just €7 a day you can enjoy a full continental breakfast served from 8am-10am every morning.
host_about:
St Christopher’s Berlin Mitte is a brand spanking new hostel located in the heart of the German capital and just minutes from the best sights and attractions Berlin has to offer. This is the perfect location for modern backpackers to explore the real Berlin's culture, history, nightlife and cuisine.  Offering new modern rooms and a fun and lively atmosphere, your European adventure begins here. 

Our hostel has brilliant transport connections to the rest of Berlin where you can get from East to West with ease using the S-Bahn (city train),  U-Bahn (underground) and tram services. There is also plenty to do around the hostel with the likes of the beautiful Museum Island just a short stroll  from the hostel and the bustling Hackescher Markt, a hub of cool restaurants, pubs and bars, perfect for a lunch time pitstop. 

To top it off we have a brand new hostel party bar, Belushi’s. Known for its epic parties, awesome club nights, live music, great food and live sports, this is one of the best backpacker party spots in the city! Hostel guests also can make the most of exclusive daily drinks deals and 25% off all food on the menu! Did we mention we have a swanky rooftop terrace too? It really is the perfect place to chill out in the summer with awesome views over Mitte. 

At our reception, book yourself onto one of our free walking tours of the city or come along on our legendary hostel bar crawls.

This is the perfect location for modern backpackers to explore the real Berlin's culture, history, nightlife and cuisine.  Offering new modern rooms and a fun and lively atmosphere, your European adventure begins here. 

Our hostel has brilliant transport connections to the rest of Berlin where you can get from East to West with ease using the S-Bahn (city train),  U-Bahn (underground) and tram services. There is also plenty to do around the hostel with the likes of the beautiful Museum Island just a short stroll  from the hostel and the bustling Hackescher Markt, a hub of cool restaurants, pubs and bars, perfect for a lunch time pitstop. 

To top it off we have a brand new hostel party bar, Belushi’s. Known for its epic parties, awesome club nights, live music, great food and live sports, this is one of the best backpacker party spots in the city! Hostel guests also can make the most of exclusive daily drinks deals and 25% off all food on the menu! Did we mention we have a swanky rooftop terrace too? It really is the perfect place to chill out in the summer with awesome views over Mitte. 

At our reception, book yourself onto one of our free walking tours of the city or come along on our legendary hostel bar crawls.

name: Cozy Spacious Gem on Lively Square in Hip Neukölln
description:
Welcome to my newly renovated historic apartment in Berlin! Since I'm often traveling myself, I open up my home in one of Berlin’s trendiest and sought-after neighbourhoods to visitors.

Located in an historic building on the most beautiful square in the neighbourhood my apartment offers views of the Herrfurthplatz and its church. It is on the ground floor, so no lugging your luggage up several flights of stairs (Berlin’s buildings are notorious for not having elevators!).
neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is located on the square at the very heart of the trendy Schiller Kiez neighbourhood. The countless cafes, bars and restaurants in the streets surrounding the square create a cosy, welcoming and vibrant atmosphere. Every Berliner’s favourite park, Tempelhofer Feld, is just 2 minutes walk from the apartment door. St Christopher’s Inns was voted ‘Best Large Hostel Chain’ in 2016.

This modest studio apartment in the center of Berlin, has been a home for us in the last 6 months.

name: Lekkerurlaub Kreuzberg - Room 1
description:
best location
gorgeous mattresses
wonderful guests
neighborhood_overview:
Our hostel is located in downtown Berlin, within the S-Bahn ring and yet far away from the well-trodden paths of the tourists. The central location between the trendy clubs of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg and the former Tempelhofer Feld airport - by the way one of the largest inner city open spaces in the world - is the perfect starting point for discovery tours to all the well known sights of the city. The subway station Schönleinstraße is only a 5 minutes walk away, the ride with underground line 8 to Alexanderplatz takes less than 10 minutes.

The Graefekiez, the area around Graefestraße at Kreuzberg, borders at the hip district of Neukölln. The neighbourhood is characterised by beautiful 19th century houses, a rather mixed population, nice cafés and bars, many small new shops, interesting galleries and restaurants. The Landwehr Canal with its banks Maybach and Paul Lincke Ufer is only a stone's throw away. Here you can sit relaxed on the shore.

Or how about a steam
host_about:
Die Räume einer ehemaligen Erste- Hilfe- Stelle in Kreuzberg wurden zu einem Gästehaus ausgebaut, der alte Charme blieb erhalten. Eingerichtet mit Objekten, die im Berliner Straßenleben zurückgelassen wurden, wie alte Hölzer, Türen und Fenster, sowie Flohmarktfundstücken.
Das Hostel "Lekkerurlaub" mit 8 Zimmern für maximal 20 Gäste ist inhabergeführt.
Ebenerdig gelegen, betrittst du unseren Aufenthaltsraum, daran schließen sich die Zimmer, Duschen und WCs an.

Berlinbücher, Reiseführer und Stadtpläne stehen zur Verfügung.
W-Lan ist frei.
Da wir keine 24 Stunden Rezeption haben, bitten wir darum, die Check- in Zeiten zu respektieren.

Solltest du dich verspäten, gib uns umgehend per Mail oder Telefon Bescheid.
Auf der Straße sind öffentliche, kostenlose Parkplätze verfügbar.
Bei schönem Wetter kannst du deinen Kaffee auf typische Berliner Art auf dem Trottoir vor der Tür genießen.

It's an honest place, elegant in its simplicity, full of art and colors, with a big garden on the back. The flat is part of Gaswerksiedlung - one of the latest and most interesting complexes of creative studios in town - located slightly out the city's Ring, five minutes of walk away from Funkhaus Berlin.
neighborhood_overview: Whether this is a pretty quiet neighborhood, so much is happening! Besides hosting some of the most interesting concerts of contemporary classic and electronics and Monom's unique immersive 4D sound system space, Funkhaus offers itself as a great location to get in touch with Berlin's history during the Cold War and with the Spree river's waters and nature - there you can rent a kayak or a Stand-Up Paddle! You can also have an amazing pizza at Zola and German or Italian specialties at the Milchbar. In our building there's Flow - a lovely cafeteria, hang out and lunch space. The nearest supermarket is just a few minutes away, as well as one of the biggest, most known and colorful clubs in town: Sisyphos. If you want to have a nice walk, the bay of Rummelsbucht can offer really a lot and give you a good insight into the daily lives of those Berliners who prefer to live in between the area's quietness and our lovely big city's mess. The whole city is still completely at hand!

Another well-known landmark of Steglitz is the Steglitz Town Hall, which was built in the neoclassical style and is an impressive example of 19th century architecture.

For nature and garden lovers, the Berlin Botanical Garden is a worthwhile attraction. The garden covers an area of over 43 hectares and is home to more than 22,000 plant species from all over the world.

description:
Spacious, high-ceilinged apartment on the first floor of a lovely Altbau in a quiet neighbourhood.

Situated only a moment from a serene waterway walk that leads to good places: Schlossgarten (West); Zoologischer Garten (East); Reichstag (East).
host_about:
I am a wannabe triathlete, marathon runner, non-car commuter. These pursuits (for now) happily occupy me and my thoughts. I am also very interested in pondering the arts, ethics, politics and philosophy. Recently, I have taken an interest in classical music and opera.

My favourite destinations are some European cities which feel familiar but inspiring: Rome, Paris, Barcelona and Bologna. Places where a long wander can  offer up new possibilities, plenty of ideas and enchantments.

The books on my shelf, read or otherwise, are a mix of aspirational novels (Proust, Pynchon), aspirational textbooks (teach yourself Java!) and easier reading thoughtful stuff from the likes of Julian Barnes, John le Carré, Alan de Botton, Edmund White, Bertrand Russell. Travel guides, pop science etc. Last year I read Raymond Monk's biography on Wittgenstein and it made its mark on my outlook. Of course, there are also some sports books on the shelf too... I am a bit of a geek in many ways.

I moved to Berlin from London in May 2016. Whilst Berlin has long had reputation for being a clubber's paradise -  and the catchphrase "poor but sexy" does seem to apply - it has developed into a city that offers so much, and so effortlessly, that the city's appeal for me is quite different from its traditional labels. For example: the proximity to green & quiet spaces; the cycling; the international start-up scene, the range of culinary options, the variety of sports clubs and halls... in short: the quality of life & style astounds me.

Entdecken Sie ein schillerndes Ambiente zwischen Kitsch und Gemütlichkeit in einem gediegenen Berliner Altbau. Der ideale sehr zentrale Ausgangspunkt, um die turbulente Hauptstadt Berlin zu erkunden. Frühstücksbuffet und Kinderbetreuung zusätzlich buchbar.

neighborhood_overview: Welcome to Wedding, the vibrant neighborhood that truly embodies the authentic Berlin experience. With its raw, industrial charm, Wedding boasts a unique energy that has yet to succumb to tourist traps. Art nouveau buildings from the 1930s sit alongside abandoned factories that have been repurposed into music venues, independent galleries, and clubs. Explore the flea market at Leopold Platz or check out the famous Mauerpark. Catch a show at Silent Green, a former crematory transformed into a music hall, or see what's on at Panke Culture, an alternative club and cultural center housed in a former factory. These are just a few examples of the many things to see and do in Wedding. Discover more by reading Time Out's article about Wedding, and don't hesitate to ask me for insider tips. Join the many who have fallen in love with Berlin's unique charm since the fall of the Wall.

name: Westendperle am Olympiastadion
description:
The Westendperle is within walking distance of the Olympic Stadium, the Waldbühne and the Messe Berlin. 
In an unbeatable location in the heart of Charlottenburg-Westend, you can expect a cozy apartment in the attic's capital.
The Westendperle is a quiet oasis in the countryside and at the same time offers a close connection to the most popular places in Berlin.
neighborhood_overview:
Within walking distance of the Westendperle, you will find the Teufelsberg with its famous septic system, which has a unique history to tell as a relic of the cold war and is one of the main attractions in Berlin. At the same time, it's one of the largest street art galleries in the world. 

In a few minutes you are already on the platform of the Teufelsberg and can enjoy a free all-round view over Berlin. Take a picnic blanket and watch the Berlin skyline is illuminated by the dazzling colors of the sunset.

This atmosphere is unforgettable and offers the perfect balance to the exciting capital. 

In summer days, a trip to the small beach on the Havel River is worthwhile, which can be reached by car or bus in just 5 to 10 minutes. A day trip to the Peacock Island is recommended – an island with a castle built by Friedrich Wilhelm II, colorful free-roaming peacocks and numerous exotic plants. 

The Westendperle offers the best of two worlds.

name: Feel at home in Berlin Friedrichshain!
neighborhood_overview:
Berlin Friedrichshain (Fhain) is one of the famous Berlin neighborhoods (we call them "Kieze" here). While our street is quiet (dead end - no car traffic), the Kiez itself is full of bars, nightlife and cute little owner-operated stores. Friedrichshain used to be known for its punk scene - nowadays there is a pleasant mix of young people, old established Berliners, students, creative and alternative minds and young families.
There is a large organic supermarket around the corner, but honestly, there are so many delicious and inexpensive restaurants nearby that you will probably prefer these.

Boxhagener Platz - 5 min walk.
Simon-Dach-Str. - 2 min walk.
Alexanderplatz - 10 min with U5.
Museum Island - 15 min U5.
Brandenburg Gate - 15 min with U5.
Central station - 18 min with U5.

Neukölln is a lively, multicultural neighbourhood, not far from the city centre, with the apartment nestled right in middle of all the best spots!

Weserstr. (5 min walk away), is famous for its many bars and eclectic restaurants, and also has many cute boutiques, vintage stores, local galleries + small independant cinemas showing foreign films.

The canal is a short stroll away and is a popular hangout, especially in the summertime - grab a beer from the 'spati'b and find a spot to people watch.

Templehofer feld is large park on the former Tempelhof airport 25 min walk away, sunsets up here are gorgeous and if you have an interest in history and architecture, I'd recommend catching a guided tour of the old airport.

And I'm very happy to offer recommendations if needed - from the best döner kebab, bars, restaurants, events happening during your stay to my own fave spots in the city.

Like hardly any other city, it offers a variety with over 150 concert houses, theaters and stages, 3 opera houses, countless cinemas and about 170 museums.

Berlin has always been thrilling. In recent years, the metropolis has become a magnet for visitors and is one of Europe's most popular destinations. Get fascinated by the unique energy of the capital!

All rooms at the Hotel Ambiente Berlin feature cable TV, a refrigerator and a private bathroom with a shower as standard. A free internet terminal is available in the lobby.

A breakfast buffet is available every morning from 07:00 to 10:00 in the bright breakfast room of the Hotel Ambiente, which is decorated with colorful paintings. The hotel also has a supermarket and there are many bars and cafes nearby.

description:
The flat is located in a quiet and elegant street in the historic Prenzlauerberg district.

In the immediate vicinity is the Max-Schmelling-Halle, venue for numerous famous events and concerts, the colourful and vibrant Mauerpark, a vital centre for music, street performers and antiques, the Kulturbrauerei, the memorial of the Berlin Wall and famous museums.

Trendy cafés, pubs, restaurants, bars and clubs turn day into night and make this district an ideal place to stay in Berlin.
neighborhood_overview:
Characterised by green streets and parks, elegant 20th-century historical buildings, Prenzlauer Berg is home to young professionals and affluent families.

Gleimviertel is a quiet residential section of the Prenzlauer Berg district, known for its renovated 20th-century apartment blocks, cafés and trendy shops. Mauerpark, which includes part of the Berlin Wall that once divided the park in two, hosts a popular Sunday flea market as well as rock concerts and sports events at the Max-Schmeling-Halle.

Just a five-minute walk away is the famous 'Colosseum' cinema, which dates back to the end of the 19th century.
The road to it offers a variety of restaurants with international cuisine and numerous historic "kneipe" and bars.

description:

neighborhood_overview:
Discover Friedrichshain, Berlin’s vibrant and eclectic neighborhood known for its dynamic blend of history, culture, and modernity.

❤️ Don't miss Boxhagener Platz, affectionately known as "Boxi", a charming square at the heart of the neighborhood.

Berlin-Mitte is a fascinating area with many historical and cultural highlights. Here are some of the most notable attractions:

Museum Island: A UNESCO World Heritage Site, Museum Island is home to an impressive collection of museums, including the Pergamon Museum, the Neues Museum, the Altes Museum, the Bode Museum and the Alte Nationalgalerie.

Alexanderplatz: Alexanderplatz is a central square in Berlin-Mitte and an important transport hub. It is known for the Berlin TV Tower and the Weltzeituhr clockwork. Alexanderplatz is also a popular meeting place and shopping area with shops, restaurants and cinemas.

Berlin Cathedral: Berlin Cathedral is a magnificent Protestant church and a landmark of the city. Visitors can visit the cathedral, admire the impressive architecture and climb the dome to enjoy a breathtaking view of Berlin.

Unter den Linden: The magnificent boulevard Unter den Linden stretches from the Brandenburg Gate to Schlossplatz.

host_about:
Hi, 

ich bin Susanne und wohne mit meinen beiden Kindern in Königstein Falkenstein am Taunus. Wir lieben diesen Ort, weil er die perfekte Mischung zwischen Stadtnähe (20KM bis Frankfurt), Anbindung ans Rhein-Main-Gebiet und ruhiger Natur bietet. An unserem Gartenzaun beginnt das Naturschutz- und Heilklimagebiet Taunus, mit wunderbaren Wander-, Rad- und Sportmöglichkeiten. Diese Landschaft wird seit über 2.000 Jahren bewohnt und bietet daher außergewöhnliche historische Erkundungsmöglichkeiten von keltischen Ringwällen, römischen Kastellen bis zu den Burgen des späten Mittelalters. 

Ich selbst reise schon seit vielen Jahren mit Airbnb und genieße die spannenden Begegnungen mit verschiedensten Gastgebern. Gern laden wir jetzt auch Gäste zu uns ein und freuen uns auf Euch!

Beruflich beschäftige ich mich mit dem Thema Energiewende, Energieeffizienz und Optionen der Sektorkopplung. Dies beinhaltet auch viele Dienstreisen, so dass ich nicht immer zu Hause bin, sondern den Schlüssel zu Eurer Wohnung auch manchmal am Haus hinterlege. Telefonisch könnt Ihr mich aber gern erreichen.

Mit herzlichen Grüßen

Susanne

Historical and Cultural Attractions:

East Side Gallery
Just a short walk away, this world-famous open-air gallery displays over 100 murals painted directly on the longest remaining stretch of the Berlin Wall. It’s a must-see for anyone interested in Berlin's history and street art culture.

RAW-Gelände
A former train repair yard turned alternative cultural complex. By day, you’ll find skateparks, flea markets, and climbing walls. By night, it transforms into a hotspot with clubs, bars, and concert venues - a key destination for those wanting to experience Berlin’s legendary nightlife.
